# Change record: 2026-10-18-round-17-skill-per-machine

*Generated by `spec` from the YAML file beside it. Don't edit this file by hand.*

*2026-10-18 · code-first · target: python · closed 2026-10-18*

**Request (summarized):** Install the skill and the subagents once per machine, as links in the user-level folders to the installed toolkit, instead of copying them into each repository

## Open decisions, most consequential first

None.

## Changes to the spec

- **add DR-53 (The skill and subagents are installed once per machine,…)**: the engineer chose the user-level location in round 17.
  - title: The skill and subagents are installed once per machine, as links to the installed toolkit
  - decided_by: agent
  - elements: CLI, AGENT
  - requirements: CLI-9, CLI-21, AGENT-42
  - recorded: round 17
  - context: With a copy of the skill in every repository, an update to the toolkit reached a repository only when someone ran setup there and committed the result, and a repository's copy could disagree with the `spec` installed on the machine. The engineer asked how updates would reach their other repositories, and chose the user-level location.
  - decision:
    `spec init` links the user-level folders to the installed toolkit: ~/.claude/skills/syseng and the two subagents in ~/.claude/agents for Claude Code, and ~/.hermes/skills/syseng for Hermes when Hermes is set up on the machine.
    - With an editable install, an edit to the toolkit reaches every repository at once. Otherwise, upgrading the toolkit does.
    - A repository keeps its spec, the instruction-file section, and Claude Code's hook script and settings. Setup removes the copies earlier setups put in repositories.
    - A skill or subagent of the engineer's own at those paths is left alone.
    - Antigravity, with no user-level folder known, still gets a copy in the repository.
  - alternatives: A copy per repository, refreshed by setup and flagged when stale, which keeps each repository self-contained at the cost of a commit per update per repository. A Claude Code plugin, which DR-1 ruled out.
  - consequences: The skill an agent follows always matches the `spec` command it describes. A machine needs the toolkit installed and setup run once before its sessions get the skill. Claude Code's cloud sessions don't read user-level skills.
- **modify DR-38 (The skill ships inside the package, and setup installs…)**: DR-53 installs the skill once per machine.
  - status: superseded in round 17 by DR-53 on where the skill is installed. Its rules for the skill's content still hold.
- **modify CLI-21 (Setup shall install the skill and the subagents once…)**: DR-53.
  - text: ~~Setup shall keep one copy of the skill in a repository, whichever harnesses the repository uses.~~ → Setup shall install the skill and the subagents once per machine, as links to the installed toolkit, instead of copying them into repositories.
  - why: ~~copies drift apart and make a reviewer wonder which one is real. The engineer noticed two copies and asked whether the skill was duplicated.~~ → copies drift apart and fall behind the toolkit. The engineer noticed two copies of the skill, asked how updates would reach their other repositories, and chose the user-level location.

  - text: ~~The CLI shall set up a repository in one command, writing the spec skeleton where none exists, the skill, and the hooks and subagents for each harness the engineer names.~~ → The CLI shall set up a repository in one command, writing the spec skeleton where none exists and the hooks for each harness the engineer names, and linking this machine's user-level folders to the toolkit's skill and subagents.
  - *Acknowledged CLI-V5 (Setting up an empty repository writes a spec that…):* still holds: setup writes the skeleton and hooks; the skill now comes from the user-level links, which CLI-V12 checks

  - *Acknowledged DR-52 (Agents and hooks run the toolkit as `spec` from…):* unaffected: agents still run spec from the PATH

Setup records the harnesses, and running it again with them changes nothing.~~ → Setup links the machine's user-level skill and subagent folders to the installed toolkit and copies nothing into the repository.
